prompt:
Research the official rate limits of the public GitHub REST API for unauthenticated and authenticated requests. Cite the GitHub documentation page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The official rate limits for the GitHub REST API differ based on whether the request is authenticated or unauthenticated, and further depend on the type of authentication used (Personal Access Token vs. GitHub App). Below are the specific limits for the core REST API endpoints.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For requests using a personal access token (classic) or OAuth, the rate limit is 5,000 requests per hour per user." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests using a Personal Access Token (classic) or OAuth have a rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For unauthenticated requests, the rate limit allows for up to 60 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 requests per hour.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For requests made with a GitHub App, the rate limit is 15,000 requests per hour per installation." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests made via a GitHub App are limited to 15,000 requests per hour per installation.
